title: Anthropic S-1
author: SiNTEx
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。

comments.author: trjordan
comments.textRawHtml:
Everything comes back to whether the demand is really there.

Anthropic thinks it is. The got the demand / datacenter match right in Q2, got great margins, and committed hard.

They've got:

- $114b committed to Google

- $110b committed to AWS

- $161b committed to Broadcom

- $120b committed to SpaceX

If the party continues, they'll go from $50b in revenue to $500b and be fine.

But if they don't, it's going to hurt. And that's their only choice, because otherwise, they end up with a frontier model and 50% of the capacity and get eviscerated on either availability or last-minute datacenter leases.

It's a big business, but it's not an easy business.

children.author: Maxatar
children.textRawHtml:
These commitments aren't annual though, most of them amount to 10 billion a year commitments for 10 years. Put another way Anthropic has committed 52 billion dollar a year to these companies and their S-1 indicates they earn 67.2B a year in revenue.

I'm not going to predict whether Anthropic succeeds or fails, just that it's very misleading to claim that Anthropic needs to grow to $500b in revenue without making it clear that it's $500B in revenue per decade rather than $500B in revenue per year which is what most people reading such a number would assume.

children.author: Silhouette
children.textRawHtml:
Surely the thing the AI giants fear the most in this respect must be the possibility that competitive open models and locally available hardware reach the point of viability for most people. If that happens then where is the moat for the giants?

If progress with frontier models doesn't continue at the same pace then the investments and funny money deals might start to look very fragile.

If progress does continue then that progress might be towards smaller models more than quantum steps up in quality or capability that would increase the risk of the scenario above.

All of this is set against a backdrop of public hostility and political problems that I can only imagine increasing in the near term as well.

This feels like an unusually high stakes game of poker. I don't think I'd want to bet on Big AI right now if I had a few billion lying around. Then again - maybe that's why I don't have a few billion lying around!
children.textZhHtml:
毫无疑问，人工智能巨头在这方面最担心的一定是竞争性开放模型和本地可用硬件可能达到大多数人的生存能力。如果发生这种情况，那么巨头们的护城河在哪里？

如果前沿模型的进展不能以同样的速度继续下去，那么投资和滑稽的资金交易可能会开始显得非常脆弱。

如果进展继续下去，那么这种进展可能会朝着更小的模型发展，而不是质量或能力的量子进步，这会增加上述情况的风险。

所有这一切都是在公众敌意和政治问题的背景下进行的，我只能想象这些问题会在短期内也是如此。

这感觉就像一场异常高风险的扑克游戏。如果我有几十亿美元的话，我想我现在不会想押注于大人工智能。话又说回来——也许这就是为什么我手头没有几十亿的原因！

children.author: Silhouette
children.textRawHtml:
I've made that same point myself in the past. It's more of an accidental moat though - and not one they can defend for very long if they're no longer getting value out of those components themselves.

I saw an interesting observation the other day that Jensen Huang has played this game the best because his company is the one actually selling real products and making real money in return. If all the AI giants are buying up huge amounts of hardware speculatively because they assume they will need those data centres in the future and then the bottom falls out of the market then it's the AI companies left holding the baby. And if we do get to a point where local models are competitive then the OpenAIs and Anthropics of the industry might face real difficulties but it would just be a different market for Nvidia to also be selling real hardware and still in exchange for real money.
children.textZhHtml:
我自己过去也曾表达过同样的观点。不过，这更像是一条意外的护城河 - 如果他们不再从这些组件本身中获取价值，那么他们就无法长期捍卫这条护城河。

前几天我看到一个有趣的观察，黄仁勋在这个游戏中玩得最好，因为他的公司是真正销售真实产品并赚取真金白银的公司。如果所有人工智能巨头都投机性地购买大量硬件，因为他们认为未来将需要这些数据中心，然后市场触底，那么剩下的就是人工智能公司。如果我们确实达到了本地模型具有竞争力的地步，那么该行业的 OpenAI 和 Anthropics 可能会面临真正的困难，但对于 Nvidia 来说，这将是一个不同的市场，它也可以销售真正的硬件，并且仍然可以换取真正的金钱。

children.author: vlovich123
children.textRawHtml: Training costs haven’t plummeted like they have for inference afaik and the efficiencies are just translated into running larger and longer training. Basically Jevon’s paradox in action just like on the inference side.
children.textZhHtml: 训练成本并没有像推理那样大幅下降，而且效率只是转化为运行更大、更长的训练。基本上，杰文悖论在行动中就像在推理方面一样。

children.author: mike_hearn
children.textRawHtml: That's already happened. It's one reason prices have dropped so much lately (n.b. in the quarter that's not in their S-1, I think!) They've been able to improve model efficiency a lot through better algorithms and training models to be less verbose.
children.textZhHtml: 这已经发生了。这是最近价格大幅下跌的原因之一（注意，我认为是在 S-1 之外的季度！）他们已经能够通过更好的算法和训练模型来减少冗长，从而大大提高模型效率。

children.author: pierreb-aiva
children.textRawHtml:
Jevon’s paradox would apply. If I can use order(s) of magnitude more AI for the same price, I would absolutely do that. It would also unlock many use cases that are currently gated by model pricing, which is largely dictated by the price of compute + frontier intelligence markup.

And thats just the inference side of things. For training, the big players like Anthropic would still be able to benefit from cheaper compute, by generating more RL rollouts, running more RL environments, and thus still providing frontier intelligence that would justify the markup.

Many customers cancelling would only be a risk if the compute expenditure was more decentralized. But its not
children.textZhHtml:
杰文悖论适用。如果我能以相同的价格使用更多数量级的人工智能，我绝对会这么做。它还将解锁目前受模型定价限制的许多用例，而模型定价很大程度上取决于计算+前沿智能标记的价格。

这只是事物的推理方面。对于训练，像 Anthropic 这样的大公司仍然能够从更便宜的计算中受益，通过生成更多的 RL 部署、运行更多的 RL 环境，从而仍然提供证明加价合理的前沿情报。

如果计算支出更加去中心化，许多客户取消只会带来风险。但事实并非如此

children.author: solyin
children.textRawHtml: The question is, how're those datacenters build outs coming along? two reasons for Anthropic to cancel those contracts. A) They don't need the capacity because they have capacity elsewhere, or b) they don't need the capacity because no one is using Claude. (I guess c) they don't need the capacity because theyre running Claude more efficiently is also technically possible.) For B to happen, they've got the demand in the form of contracts, and models don't really seem like they're shrinking, though there's a lot of non-public info, Astra > insize than sol, and Opus > insize than a Sonnet. So then we're looking at situation A), and the think to look at is SpaceX has the vertical integration to be able to plonk down datacenters and get them powered with literal jet/rocket engines/turbines that they make from scratch because they're a space rocket company when no on else can. So, personally, I don't think it's that big a risk to SpaceX's revenue. Or rather, is cancelable in 90 days, but smart money is going to see those cancelations coming from a lot longer away, if you're tracking datacenter construction. (Disclaimer, I picked up some SPCX; not financial advice, etc)

children.author: burnerRhodov3
children.textRawHtml:
I don't know why I'm responding to this, because I suspect this isn't being argued in good faith, but let's actually look at the numbers.

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), in 2024:

- *Texas natural gas production:* 27.5 billion cubic feet per day. - *Texas natural gas consumption:* 14.6 billion cubic feet per day.

So Texas produces nearly twice as much natural gas as it consumes domestically.

Natural gas contains approximately 1,025 BTU per cubic foot. Assuming 50% efficiency in a natural gas power plant, and 1 kWh equals 3,412 BTU.

27.5 − 14.6 = *12.9 billion cubic feet per day.*

12.9 billion × 1,025 BTU × 50% efficiency ÷ 3,412 BTU/kWh ÷ 24 hours = *approximately 80.7 GW of continuous electrical generation.*

That's the equivalent of more than EIGHT 10-GW AI computing campuses operating around the clock.

Lastly, a significant amount of natural gas is produced alongside crude oil. When producers can't economically capture or transport that gas, some of it is burned off through a process called flaring. Those flames you sometimes see at oil and gas facilities are an example, although refinery flares also serve important safety functions.

Seems like you just like to say snarky things about Elon, but can't be asked to do any actual math.
children.textZhHtml:
我不知道为什么要对此做出回应，因为我怀疑这并不是出于善意的争论，但让我们实际看看这些数字。

根据美国能源信息管理局 (EIA) 的数据，2024 年：

- *德克萨斯州天然气产量：* 每天 275 亿立方英尺。 - *德克萨斯州天然气消耗量：* 每天 146 亿立方英尺。

因此，德克萨斯州生产的天然气几乎是国内消耗量的两倍。

每立方英尺天然气含有约 1,025 BTU。假设天然气发电厂的效率为 50%，1 kWh 等于 3,412 BTU。

27.5 − 14.6 = *129 亿立方英尺/天。*

129 亿 × 1,025 BTU × 50% 效率 ÷ 3,412 BTU/kWh ÷ 24 小时 = *约 80.7 GW 的连续发电量。*

这相当于超过八个 10GW 的人工智能计算园区全天候运行。

最后，大量的天然气是与原油一起生产的。当生产商无法经济地捕获或运输这些气体时，其中一些气体会通过称为“燃烧”的过程燃烧掉。您有时在石油和天然气设施中看到的火焰就是一个例子，尽管炼油厂火炬也具有重要的安全功能。

似乎您只是喜欢说一些关于埃隆的尖酸刻薄的话，但不能要求您做任何实际的数学计算。

children.author: jordanb
children.textRawHtml:
I honestly think that the whole Memphis/Colossus debacle is what lead to the datacenter backlash. Before then I'd just hear rumblings from people complaining about bitcoin miners, but data centers in general were not seen as an odious land use.

Then Elon goes to Memphis, buys a warehouse and fires up 30 jet turbines in the parking lot, and you start getting reports about the incessant noise and being able to smell it from 5 miles away.

It seems like there's a fundamental problem with realizing other people have agency and if you fuck them hard enough they will fight back.
children.textZhHtml:
老实说，我认为孟菲斯/巨像的整个崩溃是导致数据中心强烈反对的原因。在此之前，我只是听到人们抱怨比特币矿工，但数据中心总体上并不被视为令人厌恶的土地使用。

然后埃隆去了孟菲斯，买了一个仓库，并在停车场启动了 30 台喷气涡轮机，你开始收到关于持续不断的噪音的报告，并且能够从 5 英里外闻到它的味道。

意识到其他人有代理权并且如果你操他们，这似乎是一个根本问题。只要足够努力，他们就会反击。
